Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | ${e}^{3}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $3$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2x\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
